trials.notes: Used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), a single next_token() walk, get_current_depth() for subtree boundaries, get_token_type() === '#text' before get_modifiable_text(), and is_string(get_attribute('href')) to exclude missing and valueless hrefs. All called methods are documented and execution passed 8/8 with no _doing_it_wrong records.

Canonical API shape: create_fragment(), next_tag(array('tag_name'=>'a')), decoded get_attribute(), depth-bounded next_token(), and #text-only get_modifiable_text(). Lowercase tag query is documented as ASCII case-insensitive. All called methods are documented and execution passed 8/8 with no _doing_it_wrong records.

Matches the documented subtree-text recipe closely: HTML Processor for structure, next_tag('A') for openers, string-valued href filtering, >= depth guard, and #text-only decoded text collection. All called methods are documented and execution passed 8/8 with no _doing_it_wrong records.

failure_analysis: All trials passed every hidden case, so there are no failed-case misconceptions to diagnose. The docs did well on the key decisions for this task: they explicitly direct DOM-style subtree text extraction to WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), document get_current_depth() with the >= boundary rule, warn that next_token() otherwise walks to the end, say to append only #text tokens for ordinary text, and state that get_attribute() and get_modifiable_text() return decoded strings. The get_attribute() string|true|null contract also prevented the valueless-href case from being included. Near-miss: the next_token() docs warn against nested loops for repeated regions, while the canonical solution uses an outer next_tag() loop with an inner bounded next_token() scan. The trials navigated that correctly, but the distinction could be made sharper.

doc_gaps.problem: The warning about nested token loops is broadly useful but can read as forbidding the common pattern of an outer next_tag() query plus a bounded inner next_token() subtree scan.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a sentence distinguishing unsafe nested next_token()/next_token() repeated-region loops from the safe pattern of using next_tag() to find an opener, recording its depth, then consuming that element's subtree before continuing the next_tag() search.

doc_gaps.problem: The HTML Processor section delegates most attribute semantics to the Tag Processor section, even though structured extraction tasks often use get_attribute() through WP_HTML_Processor.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Inline a compact example in the HTML Processor get_attribute() section showing missing attributes return null, valueless boolean attributes return true, empty valued attributes return '', and normal values return decoded strings.

doc_gaps.problem: The recipe says ordinary text is #text tokens and special elements are opt-in, but it does not explicitly mention links/anchors as a typical subtree-text use case.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add anchors to the examples of ordinary DOM-style text extraction, emphasizing that markup inside the element contributes no text, images contribute no alt text unless a caller explicitly implements that policy, and character references are already decoded.
